author: Pete Fiutak
title: LSU vs SE Louisiana Prediction: Is This When the Tigers Get the Offense Going? - NewsBreak
text:
By Pete Fiutak ,
1 hours ago No, Brian Kelly wasn’t right to go off on the first question in the post-game press conference after a 20-10 win over Florida, but he had a wee bit of a point.
LSU is 3-0, it beat Clemson to start the season, took down the Gators in a tough SEC opener, and none of that was noticed because the offense has been so mediocre.
If Kelly and the Tigers want to prove a point, and if they want to get the O going before next week’s likely shootout at Ole Miss, this is the game to do it.
SE Louisiana lost to Louisiana Tech 24-0 to start the season - LSU beat the Bulldogs 23-7 in Week 2 - but the offense got going in two straight wins.
LSU Tigers vs SE Louisiana Lions Game Preview Sep 13, 2025; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers quarterback Garrett Nussmeier (18) against the Florida Gators during the second half at Tiger Stadium. © Stephen Lew-Imagn Images
LSU vs SE Louisiana How To Watch Saturday, September 20, 2025
Game Time: 7:45 PM ET
TV: SEC Network
Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA
@PeteFiutak
Why SE Louisiana Will Win The Lions know how to move the ball.
They might not have a high-powered offense, but they do a good job creating easy third down chances, and they control the clock.
Throw in a great pass rush to go along with the attack that ramped it up over the last few weeks, and ...
Why LSU Will Win The offense is about to dominate.
And no, it won't be cranking it up because head coach Brian Kelly had a silly rant after the Florida win, but it will do it because it has to open it up a bit. The defense will take care of the rest.
LSU isn't Murray State or Mississippi Valley State.
With Ole Miss up next, the Tigers have to get the offensive line working already. The ground really isn't good so far. The passing game hasn't been dangerous enough.
It's about to show off in this, helped by three takeaways from the defense, but ...
LSU Will Be Workmanlike in Its Tune-Up There will be a fine line between not wanting to show Ole Miss any sort of a new wrinkle that hasn't been there over the first three games, and getting this thing going already. The easy way to do that is to pound away on the ground.
The Tigers will run 40 times, things will start to break through after the first few drives, and there won't be any issues, even if it isn't a dynamic performance.
